sources.entry: Build A Native Desktop App with JS

summary.title: How to build native desktop apps with JavaScript (Proton Native)
summary.one_liner: You learn how to scaffold a React-style desktop app with Proton Native and build a small window that hashes typed text to MD5.
takeaways: Proton Native is described as React Native for desktop, compiling to native platform code rather than running on Chromium like Electron.
Set up a project with npm install -g create-proton-app and create-proton-app my-app; Windows needs windows-build-tools and Linux needs libgtk-3-dev and build-essential.
Build UI with App, Window, Box, Text and TextInput components; Window takes title, size and menuBar props.
Use Node's crypto module to compute an MD5 hash of text, updating component state on each TextInput onChange event.
The author notes Proton Native was in its infancy at the time, was buggy, and did not support styling yet.
summary.summary: The article introduces Proton Native, a React-based framework for building desktop apps that render to native widgets instead of a web view. It walks through installing platform prerequisites, generating a project with create-proton-app, and reviewing the index.js file. The example is a small class component with a TextInput whose onChange handler stores the text in state and displays its MD5 hash, computed with Node's crypto module. The author warns that the framework was early-stage, buggy, and lacked styling at the time of writing.
